candidates.speaker: Eric Schnapper

Holding (from CAP text): an unpleaded affirmative defense may be considered when the plaintiff was not unfairly surprised or prejudiced; 'the general rule is that ... a party waives its right' but the liberal pleading rules mean that 'when the failure to raise an affirmative defense does not prejudice the plaintiff, it is not error for the trial court to hear evidence on the issue.' The Eleventh Circuit quotes this at 842 F.2d at 263 (App. 9-10 of the petition appendix).
